## 開篇：固定收益市場主線

AI交易原本有個好開局，隨後股市再度全面下挫，帶動美國公債上漲，以短天期表現最強。2年期殖利率下降4.24個基點至4.7618%，10年期下降2.22個基點至5.0461%。Anthropic募資規模創下紀錄，上市首日表現也亮眼，仍未能恢復市場對整個AI擴張融資鏈的信心，美國高收益債利差明顯擴大。

美國就業與製造業數據轉弱之際，聯準會維持緊縮的理由也增加。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee仍認為12月可以討論較大幅度升息，並警告AI投資可能超過經濟短期所能供應的產能。副主席Philip Jefferson則區分了當前投資需求推升通膨的影響，以及日後可能出現的生產力效益。美債這波漲勢主要來自實質殖利率下降；油價回升之下，通膨補償僅小幅降低。

各筆融資的結果，也讓取得資金與資金價格的差別更加鮮明。Alphabet完成加拿大債券發行，兩筆與該公司相關的市政預付能源融資卻因需求及定價問題延後。市場追捧頂尖AI實驗室的股票，同時也對整體基礎建設擴張所需的信用融資提出更高要求。

## 美債走強，數據分歧與聯準會鷹派訊號並存

短天期美債漲幅優於長天期，殖利率曲線因而轉陡。5年期殖利率下降3.06個基點至4.8571%，30年期僅下降0.53個基點至5.4046%。2年與10年期利差擴大2.02個基點至28.43個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大3.71個基點至64.28個基點。相較於對政策利率敏感的天期，長期借款成本當日獲得的緩解小得多。

拉長至一週，美債也有所回升。相較11月12日，2年期殖利率低11.96個基點，10年與30年期分別低8.1及4.75個基點。不過，與一個月前相比，2年期僅下降1.01個基點，10年期則下降9.36個基點。近期短天期反彈的幅度雖較大，但放在較長一段時間的調整中，短期殖利率仍接近一個月前水準。

10年期殖利率當日降幅大多來自實質殖利率。TIPS殖利率下降1.8個基點至2.8527%，損益兩平通膨率下降0.42個基點至2.1934%。一個月的分解結果卻很不同：實質殖利率上升6.97個基點，通膨補償下降16.33個基點。這段期間名目殖利率下降，經通膨調整後的融資成本卻提高，對資本密集型企業尤其重要。

上午公布的美國數據顯示，需求與就業情勢有些轉弱。初領失業救濟金人數由20.2萬升至20.3萬，高於市場預期的19.7萬；四週平均由19萬5,750人升至19萬7,750人。續領人數的惡化更為明顯，從前值169.3萬升至176.3萬，也高於預期的171.0萬。新申請人數僅略增，但持續領取救濟金的人數上升，透露了更多就業轉弱訊息。

11月費城聯準銀行製造業指數由20.9降至6.3，遠低於市場預期的20。新訂單由4.3降至負0.4，資本支出指數由34.9降至18.9，顯示當前活動與投資意願降溫，成本壓力卻升高：支付價格指數由43.2躍升至58.2。就業指數從9.1升至11.6，未來活動指數也從33微升至33.6。這份調查反映成長動能明顯流失，但企業仍在增聘人力，投入成本的壓力也更大。

其他數據則顯示，各地工廠景氣並不一致。堪薩斯市聯準銀行11月製造業綜合指數由11升至18，另列的生產指數由16升至23。美國經濟諮商局領先經濟指標月減0.3%，市場原預期持平，前值也為持平。同時，公布的30年期房貸利率由7.11%升至7.28%，加重家庭融資負擔。

在這組好壞參半的數據中，Goolsbee週四的談話讓通膨問題更受關注。他表示，連續數月數據異常偏高，官員原先預期會改善的領域卻進展有限，因此所有政策選項都應保留。他並未承諾在12月8日至9日會議升息50個基點。Goolsbee今年沒有貨幣政策投票權，2027年將有投票權，其看法也關係到屆時決定緊縮持續多久的決策陣容。

他尤其擔心，通常會因季節性因素而降溫的月份，通膨反而增強；年初可能再度加速，因而成為他判斷政策路徑的重要因素。聯準會偏好的通膨指標9月年增3.6%，核心消費者物價也連續三個月高於預期。Goolsbee認為，關稅與能源成本上升的影響，比官員最初估計更為持久。

AI投資帶來另一股需求。路透對其談話的報導指出，Goolsbee提到規模達數兆美元的資料中心建設計畫，並質疑經濟是否有足夠的短期產能，在不增加通膨的情況下吸收這些投資。他也以Anthropic此次發行為股東帶來的流動性為例，指出財富增加可能帶動消費。地方公投若限制資料中心開發，可能改變建設速度與地點。他承認生產力有可能大幅提升，但強調其時間與規模仍不確定。

Jefferson稍早的演說，則說明在多種衝擊交疊下，政策回應須視條件而定。他指出，資料中心建設與先進運算投資已在拉高總需求及通膨；自動化和未來的生產力改善，最終可能提升潛在產出、減輕物價壓力。就業影響則可能同時包括職位遭取代與新企業出現。他沒有提出12月升息幅度的具體偏好，也沒有估計終點利率。

談到中東能源衝擊，Jefferson強調物價上漲與家庭實質所得減少的相反作用。這次衝擊發生前，通膨就已高於聯準會2%的目標；若通膨預期失去錨定，可能必須採取更強的抗通膨措施，若物價壓力受控，政策就能有較大空間保護就業。他的判斷同時考量價格上漲的來源、通膨預期及勞動市場狀態。

聯準會理事Michael Barr另表示，通膨仍過高，政策需要進一步調整。他也警告，擬議中的銀行監理變動，累積起來可能削弱聯準會辨識金融脆弱性的能力。Barr在2025年初卸下監理主管職務後仍留任理事；他說，華盛頓總部的銀行監管職位可能裁撤約三分之一，並以2007年至2009年金融危機前的人力及專業不足，說明其憂慮。接任者Michelle Bowman推動的改革，則以強化問責、減少不必要的監理負擔為目標。

另一份員工備忘錄也凸顯聯準會的成本控管。2027年最低加薪幅度訂為1%，低於各地區聯準銀行原有的3%，員工並被告知，預期加薪幅度將小於往年。這項薪酬決策是機構縮減開支的一環，Bowman也正推動將監理與監管部門人力減少約30%。

美國財政部標售$190億10年期TIPS，得標殖利率為2.903%，高於上次的2.653%。投標倍數由2.24升至2.43，最高得標殖利率的配售比例則由93.14%降至90.74%。標售殖利率較上次提高、投標倍數也改善，同日次級市場的實質殖利率則收低。

油價與當日損益兩平通膨率走勢相反。中東暴力衝突再起，持續引發供應疑慮，WTI期貨上漲0.76%至每桶$83.89，布蘭特原油也上漲0.76%至$92.65。荷蘭合作銀行的Florence Schmit表示，荷姆茲海峽通行改善，仍不足以抵銷船隻持續遭襲及美國可能發動新一輪大規模打擊的影響。Axios一名記者指出，白宮已要求五角大廈評估伊朗可能如何回應不同打擊情境。伊朗國營通訊社IRNA則報導，伊朗希望先解決荷姆茲問題，再就核議題展開接觸。

習近平、Donald Trump與Vladimir Putin在深圳同意增加成品油生產與供應。消息公布後，布蘭特原油在倫敦市場變動不大。西方官員另表示，美國再對伊朗發動一輪大規模打擊的可能性提高，其中一名官員說Trump尚未決定。沙烏地阿拉伯當局則表示，胡塞武裝攻擊利雅德金融區一棟大樓，造成損壞，無人傷亡。

需求預期也轉強。較低油價鼓勵煉油商使用配額、補充庫存，Energy Aspects、FGE NexantECA及Rystad因此將中國第四季原油進口預測上調至每日980萬至1,020萬桶。不過，歐洲柴油期貨跌至三個月低點，煉油商增產柴油的同時，也增加了汽油供應。原油與不同油品的發展不盡相同，能源前景無法僅以單一基準油價的變動概括。

美國參議院以51票對48票，否決要求政府停止對伊朗軍事行動、或取得國會授權的決議。共和黨議員Susan Collins、Lisa Murkowski及Rand Paul支持，民主黨議員John Fetterman反對。路透引述五角大廈10月下旬數據指出，衝突支出已超過$470億，比7月估計高逾25%。民主黨將於1月3日取得參眾兩院控制權，在此之前，這次表決維持了國會既有立場。

## AI融資分流：股票、公司債與市政債各有冷暖

Anthropic上市為股票融資帶來重大成功，卻未能遏止科技股全面退潮。公司與共同創辦人透過IPO及私募共籌得$1,073億，包括$813億基本發行及$260億私募；僅基本發行規模，就超過SpaceX先前$750億的紀錄。股價盤中一度突破$115，收在$97.17，較$83發行價上漲17%。

大盤隨後扭轉早盤的樂觀氣氛。那斯達克100指數回吐盤中近2.5%的漲幅，收跌2.21%；標普500下跌2.02%至7,175.83點，超過460家成分股下跌。半導體股下跌2.41%，VIX上升15.80%至28.44。Hunterbrook Capital以中國相關風險為由發布放空觀點後，AMD股價承壓，公司否認有不當行為。摩根大通、Visa與Mastercard也通報，一家供應商遭網路攻擊，部分客戶資料被存取。

Miller Tabak的Matt Maley認為，IPO成功未能消除市場對獲利能力、資本支出、利率及信用壓力的疑慮。Innovation Investor的Luke Lango則指出，投資人對頂尖前沿AI實驗室的需求，與對高負債新興雲端業者及風險較高基礎設施公司的融資意願有所不同。當日借款消息呈現了這種分歧。

Alphabet在加拿大發行C$60億、折合$42億的債券，分為四個期限，涵蓋3年至40年。其中最長天期的C$12.5億券，以高於政府債券1.85個百分點的利差定價，較初步洽談水準收窄約5個基點；浮動利率券則在承銷過程中取消。Alphabet六個月前才首次赴加拿大發債C$85億，這次再度擴大對當地市場的運用。

據Bloomberg統計，外國企業今年在加拿大的加幣發債規模已達C$540億，創下紀錄，是2025年全年的三倍以上。超大規模雲端業者帶動這波增加，但其債券同時也是加拿大投資級發行人中表現最弱的一群。這些債券讓當地投資人有更多科技業投資選擇。市場吸收的全球科技債務大幅增加，Alphabet仍能以議定條件吸引買盤。

另外兩筆與Alphabet相關的市政預付能源融資，則遇上定價障礙。兩筆合計$30億的發行因市場波動、需求不足而延後。市政債本週相對美債已變便宜，Alphabet在11月稍早也已透過一筆約$16億的預付交易取得資金。

新交易洽談條件包括一檔2039年到期券，殖利率5.15%，較AAA市政債高約138個基點；先前交易的一檔2040年到期券，利差則為111個基點。Columbia Threadneedle的Shannon Rinehart表示，部分投資人要求的利差，高於交易各方願意提供的水準，尤其當時公債正在上漲，近期又剛完成另一筆Alphabet相關交易。由高盛主辦的這些交易仍在推進。Allspring的Andy Hobbs預期，假期後不久就會重返市場，需求可望相當強勁。

對CoreWeave債券的市場估值，兩位共同創辦人以不同方式回應。Brannin McBee週三在奧斯汀的一場會議表示，將公司現金投入運算產能，報酬優於買回殖利率約15%的無擔保債券。他說，明年有13萬顆GPU的合約到期，公司有機會將已完成融資的既有基礎設施重新出租，且可按比先前更高的租金續約。

McBee比較的是債務買回與公司現金配置。CoreWeave的2032年到期、票息9.6%無擔保債券，交易價格約為面額的79%。投資人質疑其借款規模，也擔心昂貴晶片的商業使用年限，是否足以支撐相關融資；McBee則以舊硬體取得新合約，作為持續投資的依據。

另一位共同創辦人兼策略長Brian Venturo透露，他前一週以個人資金買進$3,000萬、2031年10月到期的無擔保債券，並打算持有至到期。這與McBee談到的2032年到期券不同。CoreWeave另外正尋求至少$40億的投資級貸款；Venturo的個人投資與公司擬議融資，分別反映個人信心及企業籌資安排。

SpaceX正考慮發售至少$320億債務，作為其更大規模晶片融資安排的一部分，讓AI借款計畫中預計向投資人銷售的金額更為具體。花旗銀行業務主管Viswas Raghavan表示，估計$3.5兆的AI建設，需要動用所有可用資金來源；資金選擇更嚴格，將擠壓規模較小、競爭力較弱的參與者。

亞洲的風險評估也更明確。南韓金融監管機關首次要求主要銀行、券商及保險公司，提供對AI企業的投資與放款明細。同時，在半導體出口創紀錄的帶動下，南韓年度出口首次突破$1兆。設備需求強勁，金融機構對AI的曝險也開始受到盤點。

美國國會新揭露的資料，則補充了產業貿易曝險的細節。眾議院一個委員會表示，商務部在2025年12月至2026年5月間，核准了約87.9萬顆先進AI晶片的對中出口申請，申請總量超過340萬顆。核准數量包括阿里巴巴7.5萬顆、騰訊15萬顆、百度4.3萬顆及比亞迪4,000顆，涉及輝達H200及AMD MI325X產品。

這些許可之下實際出貨多少，仍不清楚。輝達表示，許可附有嚴格條件且數量有限，之後也已停止對中國出貨H200；AMD則表示遵守美國管制。兩家公司都反駁了未遵守規定的說法。另外，Nscale若要繼續在冰島及挪威等地，讓字節跳動使用輝達GPU，就必須取得許可，遠端存取限制的商業影響因而延伸到這些設施。

信用資產表現反映風險偏好退潮。含配息計算，HYG報酬為負0.16%，LQD下跌0.07%，EMB下跌0.52%。美元指數微升0.08%至103.938，黃金期貨下跌3.05%至每盎司$3,627.90。MKS PAMP的Nicky Shiels認為，除了聯準會鷹派立場及美元走強，投資人在解除AI相關部位、因應年底流動性需求時籌措現金，也是金價承壓的部分原因。

## 全球升息訊號交織法國財政風險

歐洲官員持續主張升息，但對行動迫切性及緊縮可能造成的經濟損害，意見不盡相同。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel表示，12月升息可明確傳達將通膨帶回2%的決心。歐元區通膨目前為4%，歐洲央行已升息兩次。

Nagel認為，這次油價衝擊的嚴重程度，低於俄羅斯入侵烏克蘭後的天然氣價格飆升，目前也未見薪資與物價螺旋上升。德國通膨接近3%，遠低於四年前約10%的水準，在他看來，第二輪效應的風險因而較小。

拉脫維亞的Martins Kazaks表示，由於通膨可能擴散到其他商品及服務，可能仍須小幅升息，但會維持逐次會議判斷的方式。愛爾蘭的Gabriel Makhlouf則說，若證據持續出現，或通膨風險實現，他預期會再升息，與其先前立場一致。相較於Nagel強調12月行動的訊號意義，兩人的支持附有條件。

義大利央行總裁Fabio Panetta強調，應防止通膨根深蒂固，同時避免對成長造成不必要傷害。他支持歐洲央行目前兩次升息採取的溫和幅度，也曾承認可能需要進一步行動。義大利10月通膨意外加速至5.6%，讓遏制通膨與避免經濟受損之間的權衡，在本國格外迫切。

奧地利的Martin Kocher指出另一個可能使價格壓力延續的因素。歐洲央行估計，2026年的高溫與乾旱，可能使未來一年食品通膨增加0.3至0.8個百分點，並促成2027年第三季3.4%的預測值。奧地利央行估計，當地炎熱夏季將使2026年9月至2027年6月的整體通膨增加約0.1個百分點。科學研究也估計，夏季氣候使歐盟GDP減少約0.17%，約€170億。夏季天候的經濟影響仍在延續，同時損及產出、推高物價。

能源監管則朝放寬時程的方向推進。歐盟達成暫定協議，將石油與天然氣進口商的甲烷規範延後兩年實施，長於監管機關因戰事造成供應中斷而提出的一年延期。歐洲在兼顧能源安全與氣候相關成本之際，也調整了未來的法遵時間表。

對法國公債，Amundi的評估比匯市部位所反映的政治焦慮更為平和。投資長Vincent Mortier表示，公司對法國公債維持中立，未見恐慌性賣壓。週四10年期殖利率約4.92%，較德國公債高約150個基點；考量財政不確定性、基本面及評等，他認為這個價格合理。

若沒有災難性消息而出現更大賣壓，Mortier才可能有興趣增持。10月市場承壓時，殖利率曾達5.14%，利差達177個基點。他說，若殖利率接近5.3%，意味經通膨調整後約有3%的殖利率，將很難忽視。他對法國、比利時及義大利的債務可持續性有信心，但也批評這些國家同時存在高負債比率與公共財政赤字。

匯市投資人仍憂心法國總統大選及€3.6兆債務。Loomis Sayles全球固定收益共同主管Lynda Schweitzer表示，公司過去一個月因政治動盪建立歐元空頭部位。投機性看空部位接近2020年初以來最高。德意志銀行、摩根士丹利與德國商業銀行預測，明年歐元將至$1.08；德意志銀行也預期，隨大選風險溢價消退，年底可回升至$1.15。

這些看法背後涉及不同的政治選擇。民調領先的Marine Le Pen主張將退休年齡最低降至60歲，並減少法國對歐盟的付款；民調通常居次的Jean-Luc Melenchon則曾主張不償還部分債務。瑞穗策略師Leejun Foo警告，若法國公債壓力擴散，可能波及其他主權債市場，提高歐元區風險溢價。Amundi則認為，近期利差擴大後的價位具有可觀的買進吸引力，雙方對目前價格究竟補償了多少財政風險，確有分歧。

英國方面，英國央行決策官員Megan Greene質疑，通膨連續逾五年高於目標，是否能單以接連發生的外部衝擊解釋。她認為官員升息太慢，政策抑制需求的程度也低於預期。總裁Andrew Bailey週三則表示，伊朗衝突前，通膨原本有望在今年回到2%，兩人的說法形成對照。

英國央行本月升息25個基點至4%。投資人傾向預期12月再升息，至2月的一次升息已完全反映在價格中，並預期夏季前還有另外兩次。Greene指出，經濟比預期強、勞動市場趨穩，並警告通膨高於3%可能更受家庭注意，進而推升薪資要求。她認為，緊縮不足對政策可信度的風險，大於緊縮過度。Bloomberg對當日行情的報導顯示，德國10年期殖利率上升4個基點至3.40%，英國上升3個基點至5.31%。

日本央行總裁植田和男表示，近期消費支出下降符合預期，未改變其對消費將恢復溫和成長的看法。他預期名目薪資上升、通膨逐步放緩，將支持實質購買力。退休人士沒有薪資增加的支撐，因此較易受到物價上漲衝擊；薪資上調則正由大型企業擴散至較小企業。

東京週四的隔夜指數交換，反映12月升息機率約84%。經濟萎縮後，植田的看法仍保留了升息理由，日本央行目前正尋求讓基礎通膨維持在目標附近。更廣泛而言，Bloomberg所述利率期貨顯示，聯準會、歐洲央行及英國央行將在明年持續升息，之後至少到2031年，利率大致維持不變。科技投資、國防支出與基礎建設借款，讓資金競爭延續到遠超過下一輪政策會議的時間。

## 匯率防衛與主權融資走向分歧

南非維持利率不變，但要求進一步緊縮的委員占了相當比例。七人貨幣政策委員會中，四人支持利率維持7.25%，三人主張升息25個基點。Bloomberg調查的20位經濟學家中，19位原本預期不變。總裁Lesetja Kganyago表示，央行將評估今年兩次升息的效果，並準備在必要時再升息，使通膨回到3%目標。

決議後，蘭特回吐稍早漲幅，在新興市場貨幣普遍走弱之際，約翰尼斯堡下午5時30分時下跌1.1%；指標10年期公債殖利率當日仍下降6個基點至8.89%。從票數看，這次按兵不動所傳達的立場，比決議表面更鷹派。

決策官員列出的交疊風險，包括核心通膨上升、美元轉強、全球利率走高、燃料價格及聖嬰現象。央行用來評估風險的一項不利情境假設油價最高達每桶$130、煉油利潤空間受限，推演結果為明年通膨超過5%、成長約1%，可能需要升息兩次。另一情境假設全球殖利率與風險溢價上升、蘭特貶值，推演結果相近。Bloomberg經濟學家Yvonne Mhango仍預測2027年將降息50個基點至6.75%；Allspring的Lauren van Biljon則認為，第一季可能再有限度升息。

墨西哥週四公布的會議紀錄，讓政策分歧更為清楚。披索下跌0.9%至每美元19.03，為2025年6月以來最弱，9月初以來累計貶幅超過10%。渣打經濟學家Dan Pan表示，墨西哥央行近期降息25個基點至6.25%後，理事會多數成員大致淡化匯率疲弱的影響。美墨利差已收窄至約237個基點，創多年低點，減少了持有披索所能取得的利差收益吸引力。

持異議的Galia Borja與Jonathan Heath警告，政策可信度、通膨預期及匯率均面臨風險。Borja認為，相較其他經濟體更寬鬆的政策，可能促使市場更多利用披索對沖全球資產，放大波動。多數成員判斷核心通膨趨降，同時承認有上行風險。總裁Victoria Rodriguez曾將此次降息稱為一次性行動，並形容匯率變動有序，為進一步寬鬆的預期加上限制。CFTC數據顯示，資產管理機構的披索看空部位已達二十年最大。

巴西央行採取更直接的措施，在即期市場賣出$10億，為2024年12月以來首次此類干預。此前總統Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva表示，不急於公布新財政部長人選。雷亞爾一度收復跌幅，最終仍下跌1%，收在每美元5.94，10月大選以來累計貶值16%。2029年1月期交換利率一度上升51個基點。

Asset1的Andre Shiokawa將壓力歸因於財政疑慮，並認為央行拍賣美元是為了抑制波動與貶值速度。Persevera的Vinicius Marujo表示，干預發生在Lula談話之後，投資人轉向其他市場表達看法，反而加重交換利率的上行壓力。參議院週三支持支出限制措施，預計可使2027年初級財政收支改善500億至600億雷亞爾。然而，面對超過GDP 9%的名目赤字及超過80%的公共債務比率，投資人仍要求更大調整。

其他國家的主權借款顯示，全球波動未使所有借款人都失去市場融資管道。中國發行$20億3年期美元債，與美國公債零利差，較初步洽談約25個基點的溢酬收窄，訂單超過$680億。這是中國一年來首次發行主權美元債；雖然國際信用評等低於美國，仍重現上次零溢酬的定價。星展經濟學家Samuel Tse預期，這些債券價格將緊貼同天期美債，在全球不確定性下，對投資中國美元信用債的資金可能具有吸引力。

菲律賓睽違三年重返零售美元債市場，透過標售籌得$4.534億，3年期債券票息5.65%。公開認購最低面額為$200，持續至11月24日。國家財政主管Sharon Almanza表示，資金將支應今年預算。政府今年計畫借款2.73兆披索，2027年為3.3兆披索。

週四馬尼拉下午，披索約為每美元63.66，較上月64.20的歷史低點回升。過往零售美元債多由機構投資人認購，Almanza希望個人占比能高於上次不足10%的水準。預期這些債券的流動性將低於披索公債及國際發行債券，這是政府擴大資金來源時的一項重要特性。

對羅馬尼亞近期債券回升，花旗策略師Bhumika Gupta給予有條件的肯定。花旗持有5年期列伊債，於上個月政府獲批准之前、殖利率約7.4%時買進，目前殖利率已降至約6.8%。Gupta認為，若總理Luca Niculescu的少數政府維持穩定、落實財政計畫，包括明年赤字占GDP比率減少約1個百分點，殖利率可望朝6%移動。

三大信評機構都將羅馬尼亞列為最低投資級，展望為負向。外資持債相對GDP的比率接近十年低點，列伊今年兌歐元貶值4.8%。Gupta認為，要讓外資需求回升，財政及匯率穩定缺一不可。央行總裁Mugur Isarescu曾說，若通膨降溫趨勢可信，最早春季可開始降息；Gupta比他審慎，認為物價僵固，未來六個月寬鬆空間有限，若通膨朝預測約3.7%回落，2027年末或可有限度降息。

加彭則是在信用狀況弱得多的情況下尋求官方支持。財政部長Thierry Minko希望12月與IMF達成工作人員層級協議、1月交執董會審議。IMF表示，持續中的技術接觸可能為計畫討論鋪路，未提出時間表；政府目標與貸款機構所述進展，仍有實質差距。

債務審計將負債定為$167億，比最初估計低近五分之一，占GDP 69%，因此落在中部非洲經濟暨貨幣共同體70%的上限內。更近期的進展是，國會週三通過修正預算，預計2027年初級財政盈餘為未重訂基期GDP的0.6%，取代原擬1.3%的赤字。Minko表示，這些調整參考了與IMF工作人員的諮商；政府並預測2028及2029年盈餘將分別增至2.1%及2.5%。

Minko說，10月歐洲債券的募資已清償約€4,700萬非洲開發銀行逾期欠款，另約€1,500萬伊斯蘭開發銀行欠款也已結清，剩餘世界銀行欠款的清償作業正在收尾。加彭7月透過私募籌得$9.2億，10月公開發行籌得$5.8億，資金用於對外債務及基礎建設。

修正後架構允許最多1.04兆非洲金融共同體法郎、折合$17億的國際融資。Minko表示，再發一筆歐洲債券，是區域借款、銀行融資、專案貸款與發展援助之外的一個可能選項，尚未確定新發行金額。加彭2034年到期債券的發行殖利率為12.8%；摩根大通指數盤中數據顯示，主權利差為824個基點，在非洲僅次於塞內加爾的1,529個基點。Minko認為，投資人對非洲要求的風險溢價過高，也未充分區分國別；惠譽CCC-評等則凸顯加彭信用仍脆弱。

辛巴威採取另一條官方融資路徑，向世界銀行、非洲開發銀行及歐洲投資銀行申請贈款或貸款，以清償對這些機構本身的逾期欠款。財政部表示，配合改革及提高透明度，贈款與長期優惠融資是最可持續的選擇。該國總負債$217億，包括欠世界銀行$17億、非洲開發銀行$8.35億及歐洲投資銀行$4.33億的逾期款項。這些欠款使其無法取得新融資。先前向第三國尋求過橋融資未果，新一輪申請也尚未解決。

## 再融資與重整改變債權人的受償安排

企業交易呈現借款人取得流動性、或重新分配損失的不同方式。澳洲焦煤礦商GM3原定公開發債，因波動及利差擴大增加銷售難度，改由RRJ Capital牽頭的財團同意買進$6.19億5年期債券，募集資金將償還$6億私人信貸貸款。新券預定12月8日發行，票息9.75%，售價為面額的97%，2028年起可贖回。

這筆再融資取代的是GM3在2024年向South32收購資產時的相關融資。既有貸款由德意志銀行，以及Davidson Kempner、Farallon等私人信貸基金提供。轉為私募後，公司已按明確條件取得買方承諾，尚待正式發行。

義大利精品集團Tod's接近完成€4億銀行再融資，Della Valle家族提供附帶條件的支持承諾。擬議方案包括€2億定期貸款、€1億循環額度及€1億資本支出額度，到期日延長一年至2031年底，並重設財務契約條款。貸款銀行包括Intesa Sanpaolo、法國巴黎銀行、法國農業信貸銀行、UniCredit及Banco BPM。

若未達指定財務目標，家族將提供最多€6,000萬股權資金。Tod's表示，正與長期往來銀行敲定計畫，但未確認詳細條件。公司在2025年營收下滑7.7%至€9.664億、EBITDA減少16%至€1.447億後，提出這項增加融資彈性的方案。含租賃的淨負債為€5.78億，不含租賃為€1.22億，2024年則分別為€6.45億與€1.41億。是否納入租賃，會實質改變所呈現的債務負擔規模。

樂天在計畫發行約¥1,500億次順位債之前，面臨另一項可能推高融資成本的風險。截至11月18日，10月發行、合計¥3,600億的零售債，相對政府債券利差已擴大至約212個基點，為發行以來最高。其中2028年8月到期券，單日利差擴大12個基點，也創發行後新高。

樂天證券先前表示，多達447萬個客戶帳戶資料可能外洩，包括姓名、地址、收入及金融資產。標普11月19日指出，日本網路安全事件已對營運產生實質影響，賠償與支援成本可能明顯衝擊獲利及現金流。樂天銀行股價繼前一日跌停後，週四再跌至¥4,281。這些潛在成本，加上集團行動通訊業務持續虧損及多次仰賴債市融資，形成額外負擔。

日本菸草則量化了失去俄羅斯業務控制權所造成的損失。莫斯科接管七家子公司後，公司將認列¥1.4兆、折合$89億的損失。俄羅斯業務約占營收10%，卻占調整後營業利益四分之一；這筆損失將使集團全年轉為虧損，年末股息減半，凸顯受影響業務對獲利的重要性遠高於其營收占比。

美國結構型融資方面，Crunch Fitness安排了$8億整體業務融資，以加盟合約及智慧財產等資產支持，包括平均年限約5年的$6.5億債券、一筆可於日後動用的$1億私募票據，以及$5,000萬可變動融資額度。KBRA給予BBB-、最低投資級評等。最大部分以7.39%殖利率出售，較基準高2.5個百分點，資金擬用於再融資及營運現金準備。

這是近期一系列加盟業務支持融資之一，其他交易包括Neighborly的$2.75億發行。Crunch的總方案同時包含已發行債券與可按條件動用的額度，提供不同形式的融資能力。Guggenheim擔任唯一結構顧問及主辦簿記行，其他銀行參與銷售。

Vivid Seats公布重整方案，貸款人將取得80%股權，原股東保留約20%。債權人將提供$6,600萬第一順位擔保、優先受償的定期貸款，淨負債預計減少約$2.32億，槓桿倍數由9倍降至約3倍。知情人士指出，貸款人包括Blackstone、Shenkman、Oaktree、GDA Luma及Carlyle。

債權人在重整中取得的新債附有66%控制權變更溢價，若公司出售，須按本金166%償還。債權人將原有部位換成債務與控制權的組合，這項契約保障對其預期報酬相當重要。既有2029年到期、$3.87億定期貸款，最近報價約為面額的50%。公司股價週四盤中一度上漲105%，收漲63%。

營運背景仍艱困。第三季轉售訂單為9.7萬筆，低於逾10.4萬筆的預期，雖然調整後EBITDA為$887萬，優於預估。競爭對手大舉投入行銷，哥倫比亞特區限制轉售價格與費用的法律也將於1月生效，轉售業者正透過法院提出挑戰。另一宗事件中，知情人士表示，Scientific Games的貸款人已聘用Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher，並簽署向所有參與者開放的合作協議。

雪城Destiny USA購物中心的債務出售，凸顯既有資本結構的償付順位。開發商Pyramid Management先前對該物業$4.3億商業不動產抵押債務提出的收購價已獲接受，卻未能完成交割，之後Namdar Realty成為登記貸款人。Pyramid原擬以不到面額20%的價格買進，但該未完成報價不能用來認定Namdar的實際買價。

購物中心最近一次估價在2023年，為$1.33億，較2014年下跌81%。原獲AAA評等的最高順位CMBS券，目前交易價格約面額的17%。另有約$2.35億市政債尚未償清，以替代納稅的款項為償債來源，目前仍持續獲得付款。這些市政債早於CMBS發行，在抵押證券發售時雖然評等較低，償還順位卻更高。物業已面對零售需求疲弱、再融資成本高到難以承受的困境，市政債的優先權進一步限制抵押債券持有人的求償。

## 後續市場焦點

11月25日美東時間上午8時30分，將同時公布美國第三季GDP第二次估值與企業獲利，以及10月個人所得與支出。繼週四失業救濟及費城數據轉弱後，這組資料將更新經濟成長、企業盈餘、家庭支出及通膨狀況。對12月8日至9日FOMC會議而言，Goolsbee對季節性通膨再加速的擔憂，使物價壓力的持續性與下一次升息幅度同樣重要；Jefferson的框架則顯示，政策回應除考量當前投資需求，也取決於就業與通膨預期。

中國11月20日貸款利率決定尚待公布。路透調查28位受訪者，23位預期1年與5年期貸款市場報價利率分別維持3.00%與3.50%，五位預期其中一項或兩項調降。少數人轉而預期立即寬鬆，打破了此前數月一致預測不變的情況。若維持不變，暫停調整將延續至18個月。中國人民銀行11月稍早調整操作架構，實質上將利率走廊下限降低15個基點；花旗仍預期11月不降LPR，並預測2027年降息兩次、每次10個基點。

新的研究也為政策評估帶來較長期的就業問題。Bloomberg分析中國近1,000萬則網路徵才資訊發現，AI曝險較高的職業，其徵才降幅比曝險較低的職業多約10個百分點。這項發現的背景是官方資訊有限，企業也不願將裁員歸因於AI。在設備投資仍強之際，這對家庭需求能否持續提出了另一個問題，也是官員評估寬鬆時須面對的議題。日本週五將公布通膨，預期關鍵指標的升幅將為今年最大；植田將於11月30日發表談話，之後是12月18日政策決定。

較近期的信用觀察包括惠譽週五對加彭的評等檢視，以及菲律賓持續至11月24日的零售美元債認購。加彭仍在與IMF接觸，政府希望12月達成協議，取決於後續技術及政策進展。羅馬尼亞下一次評等檢視由惠譽在1月進行，將檢驗新政府財政計畫是否恢復可信度。南非下次排定的利率決定為1月28日。距下次會議仍有較長時間，美元、核心通膨及能源價格都可能改變官員的政策權衡；此次利率不變僅獲些微多數支持。

北美貿易談判也帶來延續至1月的成本風險。路透在美國債券交易結束後不久刊出的報導，引述11月19日加拿大諮詢簡報與會者指出，自8月談判破裂後，華盛頓在關稅減免上幾乎沒有實質讓步。加拿大鋼鐵、汽車及木材所面臨的關稅，預定2027年1月由25%升至50%。產業團體警告，若調升生效，將造成供應鏈中斷、企業關閉及失業。LeBlanc辦公室確認舉行了簡報，且持續尋求協議；與會者表示，美國期中選舉並未實質改變談判立場。

AI融資方面，延後的Alphabet相關市政債重新推出，以及SpaceX擬議債務銷售，將在投資人與結構不同的市場中檢驗需求。當天創紀錄股票發行、已完成的加拿大債券發行及延後的市政融資，結果差異鮮明，後續條件因而格外重要。能源方面，深圳增加供應的承諾，仍須落實到生產及運輸，荷姆茲周邊軍事風險也持續存在。

overall_summary.headline: 股市反轉凸顯AI融資壓力，美債上漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Anthropic上市初期的熱度隨後被全面股市賣壓取代，美國公債上漲。2年期殖利率下降4.24個基點至4.7618%，10年期下降2.22個基點至5.0461%，曲線轉陡。10年期降幅主要來自實質殖利率：TIPS殖利率下降1.8個基點，油價回升之下，損益兩平通膨率僅下降0.42個基點。美國高收益債利差明顯擴大。

續領失業救濟金人數增幅超過預期，費城製造業大幅放緩；不過，該調查的投入成本壓力升高，堪薩斯市製造業活動也增強。Goolsbee仍認為12月可討論較大幅度升息，警告AI投資可能超過經濟短期可供應的產能。Jefferson同樣區分了當前需求推升通膨的影響，以及日後可能出現的生產力效益。

Anthropic透過IPO與私募籌得$1,073億，股價收盤較發行價高17%，仍未恢復整體市場信心：那斯達克100指數回吐早盤漲幅後下跌2.21%。Alphabet在加拿大完成C$60億發債，與其相關、合計$30億的市政預付能源融資，則因需求及定價問題延後。不同結果讓能否取得資金、融資成本高低，成為AI建設的核心問題。這些市政交易重返市場，以及SpaceX可能發售債務，將進一步檢驗股票上市熱潮之外，投資人對相關債務的承接意願。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries gained as a promising start for the AI trade gave way to another broad equity selloff, leaving the strongest bond-market recovery at shorter maturities. The two-year yield fell 4.24 basis points to 4.7618% and the 10-year declined 2.22 basis points to 5.0461%. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably as Anthropic's record fundraising and successful trading debut failed to restore confidence across the companies financing the industry's expansion.

The session brought softer U.S. labor and manufacturing observations alongside fresh reasons for the Federal Reserve to remain restrictive. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee kept a larger December increase open for discussion and warned that AI investment could overwhelm near-term productive capacity. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson distinguished that immediate inflationary demand from productivity benefits that could emerge later. The resulting Treasury rally was concentrated in real yields, with only a small decline in inflation compensation as oil recovered.

Financing outcomes sharpened the distinction between access to capital and its price. Alphabet completed a Canadian bond sale while two municipal prepaid-energy offerings linked to the company were postponed over demand and pricing. Equity enthusiasm for a leading AI laboratory coexisted with more demanding credit markets for the wider buildout.

## Treasury Gains Meet Uneven Data and a Hawkish Fed

The Treasury curve steepened as the front end outperformed the long bond. Five-year yields fell 3.06 basis points to 4.8571%, while the 30-year edged down 0.53 basis point to 5.4046%. The two- to 10-year spread widened 2.02 basis points to 28.43 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap increased 3.71 basis points to 64.28. Longer borrowing costs consequently received much less daily relief than policy-sensitive maturities.

The recovery also extended across the weekly comparison. Two-year yields were 11.96 basis points below November 12, against declines of 8.1 basis points at 10 years and 4.75 at 30 years. Over a month, however, the two-year was only 1.01 basis point lower, while the 10-year had fallen 9.36 basis points. Those different horizons show the recent front-end rebound within a broader adjustment that has left short-term yields close to their month-earlier level.

Real yields accounted for most of the day's 10-year move. The TIPS yield declined 1.8 basis points to 2.8527%, while the breakeven eased 0.42 basis point to 2.1934%. The monthly decomposition remained markedly different: real yields were 6.97 basis points higher and inflation compensation 16.33 basis points lower. Lower nominal yields over that period therefore accompanied a higher inflation-adjusted financing cost, an important distinction for capital-intensive businesses.

The morning's U.S. releases offered some evidence of softer demand and employment conditions. Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 from 202,000, above the 197,000 consensus. The four-week average increased to 197,750 from 195,750. Continuing claims supplied the larger deterioration, reaching 1.763 million against expectations for 1.710 million and a previous 1.693 million. The increase in people remaining on benefits added information beyond the modest change in new applications.

November's Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index slowed to 6.3 from 20.9, well below the 20 consensus. New orders slipped to minus 0.4 from 4.3, while the capital-expenditure index fell to 18.9 from 34.9. The weakening in current activity and investment intentions came with firmer cost pressure: prices paid jumped to 58.2 from 43.2. Employment increased to 11.6 from 9.1, and future activity edged up to 33.6 from 33. The survey combined a substantial loss of momentum with continuing hiring and greater input-price pressure.

Other observations prevented a uniform reading of factory activity. The Kansas City Fed Manufacturing Composite Index rose to 18 from 11 in November, and its separate production index increased to 23 from 16. The Conference Board's Leading Economic Index fell 0.3% on the month, compared with an unchanged consensus and previous reading. Meanwhile, the reported 30-year mortgage rate rose to 7.28% from 7.11%, increasing the financing burden on households.

Goolsbee's Thursday remarks made the inflation side of that mixed picture more consequential. He said several months of unusually high readings had produced little improvement in sectors where officials expected progress, leaving all policy options open. He did not commit to a 50-basis-point increase at the December 8-9 meeting. Goolsbee does not vote on monetary policy this year but will vote in 2027, giving his assessment relevance to the coalition that will decide how long tightening continues.

He was particularly concerned that inflation had strengthened during months when seasonal patterns usually brought some cooling. The prospect of another acceleration around the beginning of the year therefore mattered to his judgment of the required path. The Fed's preferred inflation measure rose 3.6% annually in September, and core consumer prices had exceeded forecasts for three consecutive months. Goolsbee said the effects of tariffs and higher energy costs were proving more persistent than officials initially expected.

AI investment added a separate demand channel. In the Reuters account of his remarks, Goolsbee described a pipeline of data-center projects running into multiple trillions of dollars and questioned whether the economy had enough near-term capacity to absorb it without additional inflation. He also identified wealth-related consumer spending as a possible source of demand, citing the liquidity created for shareholders by Anthropic's offering. Local ballot measures restricting data-center development could affect the pace and location of construction. He acknowledged the possibility of a productivity boom while emphasizing uncertainty over its timing and scale.

Jefferson's earlier speech supplied a more conditional framework for responding to overlapping shocks. The vice chair said data-center construction and advanced computing investment were already lifting aggregate demand and inflation. Automation and future productivity improvements could eventually raise potential output and reduce price pressure, while the employment consequences could include both displacement and new businesses. He gave no numerical December preference or terminal-rate estimate.

On the Middle East energy shock, Jefferson emphasized the competing effects of higher prices and weaker real household income. Inflation was already above the Fed's 2% target when the shock arrived. An unanchoring of expectations could require a stronger inflation-focused response; contained price pressures could leave greater room to protect employment. His assessment placed the state of expectations and the labor market alongside the origin of the price increase.

Governor Michael Barr separately said inflation remained too high and further policy adjustment was needed. He also warned that prospective changes to bank supervision could cumulatively weaken the Fed's ability to identify financial vulnerabilities. Barr, who stepped down as the top supervision official in early 2025 but remained a governor, said approximately one-third of bank-regulatory positions at the Washington headquarters could be eliminated. He drew on staffing and expertise deficiencies before the 2007-2009 crisis in explaining his concern. His successor, Michelle Bowman, has pursued changes intended to improve accountability and reduce unnecessary supervisory burdens.

The Fed's own cost controls became more visible in a separate employee memo. The minimum salary increase for 2027 was set at 1%, down from 3% at the regional reserve banks, with staff told to expect smaller increases than in prior years. The compensation decision adds to institutional retrenchment that includes Bowman's effort to reduce staffing in the supervision and regulation division by about 30%.

Treasury's $19 billion 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.903%, compared with 2.653% at the previous sale. Bid-to-cover increased to 2.43 from 2.24, while allotment at the high declined to 90.74% from 93.14%. The higher auction yield and improved coverage arrived during a session in which secondary-market real yields ended lower.

Oil moved in the opposite direction from the daily breakeven decline. WTI futures gained 0.76% to $83.89 a barrel and Brent rose 0.76% to $92.65 as renewed Middle East violence sustained concern about supplies. Rabobank's Florence Schmit said improving Hormuz flows had yet to overcome the significance of continuing ship attacks and the possibility of extensive new U.S. strikes. An Axios reporter said the White House had requested Pentagon assessments of Iran's possible responses to different strike scenarios. Iran, according to state-run IRNA, wanted the Hormuz question settled before engaging on the nuclear issue.

Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin agreed in Shenzhen to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products. Brent was little changed in London following the announcement. Western officials separately said the likelihood of another round of mass U.S. strikes against Iran had increased, while one official said Trump had yet to decide. Saudi authorities reported damage, but no casualties, after a Houthi attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial district.

Demand expectations also strengthened. Energy Aspects, FGE NexantECA and Rystad raised their Q4 forecasts for Chinese crude imports to a range of 9.8 million-10.2 million barrels a day as lower prices encouraged refiners to use quotas and rebuild stocks. European diesel futures nevertheless reached a three-month low, and refiners' efforts to produce more diesel were increasing gasoline supply. These different product and crude-market developments left the energy outlook more differentiated than a single benchmark move.

The Senate voted 51-48 against a resolution requiring the administration to end operations against Iran or obtain congressional authorization. Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski and Rand Paul supported the measure; Democrat John Fetterman opposed it. Reuters cited late-October Pentagon figures putting spending on the conflict above $47 billion, more than 25% higher than the July estimate. The vote left the existing congressional stance intact ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers on January 3.

## AI Funding Divides Across Equity, Corporate Bonds and Municipals

Anthropic's debut supplied a large equity-financing success without arresting the wider retreat from technology shares. The company and its co-founders raised $107.3 billion through the IPO and a private placement, including an $81.3 billion base offering and a $26 billion placement. The base deal alone exceeded SpaceX's previous $75 billion record. Shares closed at $97.17, 17% above the $83 offering price, after briefly trading above $115.

The broader market reversed its early enthusiasm. The Nasdaq 100 erased an intraday gain of almost 2.5% and finished down 2.21%; the S&P 500 lost 2.02% to 7,175.83, with more than 460 constituents declining. Semiconductor shares fell 2.41%, and the VIX rose 15.80% to 28.44. AMD came under pressure after a Hunterbrook Capital short call citing China-related risks; the company denied wrongdoing. JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard also reported that some customer information had been accessed in a vendor cyberattack.

Miller Tabak's Matt Maley argued that the IPO's success left the market's concerns over profitability, capital spending, interest rates and credit stress unresolved. Luke Lango of Innovation Investor distinguished demand for a leading frontier laboratory from financing appetite for heavily indebted neoclouds and riskier infrastructure businesses. That distinction was visible in the day's borrowing news.

Alphabet sold C$6 billion, equivalent to $4.2 billion, of Canadian bonds in a four-part offering ranging from three to 40 years. The C$1.25 billion longest tranche priced at a 1.85-percentage-point premium to government bonds, about 5 basis points below initial discussions. A floating-rate tranche was dropped during syndication. The final transaction expanded Alphabet's use of the Canadian market six months after its C$8.5 billion debut.

Foreign-company Canadian-dollar issuance has reached a record C$54 billion this year, more than triple 2025's total, according to Bloomberg. Hyperscalers have led that increase while ranking among the weakest-performing investment-grade issuers in Canada. Their bonds have also broadened the technology exposure available to domestic investors. Alphabet's pricing showed continued demand at negotiated terms in a market absorbing substantially more global technology debt.

Two different Alphabet-linked transactions encountered a pricing obstacle. Prepaid-energy municipal offerings totaling $3 billion were postponed because of lackluster demand amid volatility. Municipal bonds had cheapened relative to Treasuries during the week, and Alphabet had already been the funding recipient on a roughly $1.6 billion prepaid deal earlier in November.

The new discussions included a 2039 maturity at a 5.15% yield, approximately 138 basis points above AAA municipal debt. The earlier transaction had included a 2040 maturity at a 111-basis-point spread. Columbia Threadneedle's Shannon Rinehart said some investors wanted more spread than the parties were prepared to offer, particularly with rates rallying and another Alphabet-linked transaction recently completed. The Goldman Sachs-managed deals remained in progress. Allspring's Andy Hobbs expected them to return soon after the holiday and anticipated relatively strong demand.

CoreWeave's co-founders offered different responses to the valuation of its debt. Brannin McBee said at an Austin conference Wednesday that investing company cash in computing capacity offered better returns than buying back unsecured bonds yielding roughly 15%. He said 130,000 GPUs would come off contract next year, creating an opportunity to lease already-funded infrastructure again. In his account, the company could recontract that capacity at higher rates than before.

The comparison concerned debt repurchases and the allocation of corporate cash. CoreWeave's 9.6% unsecured notes due in 2032 were trading around 79 cents on the dollar. Investors have questioned both the scale of borrowing and whether expensive chips will remain commercially useful long enough to justify their financing; McBee pointed to renewed contracts for older hardware in defending continued investment.

Co-founder and chief strategy officer Brian Venturo disclosed a personal $30 million purchase of unsecured bonds due in October 2031, made the previous week, and said he intended to hold them to maturity. His purchase involved a different maturity from the 2032 notes cited in McBee's discussion. CoreWeave was separately seeking at least $4 billion through an investment-grade loan. The personal investment and the proposed company financing represented distinct sources of confidence and funding.

SpaceX was considering a debt sale of at least $32 billion as part of its larger chip-financing arrangement, adding a more specific prospective distribution amount to the industry's borrowing pipeline. Citi's head of banking, Viswas Raghavan, said the estimated $3.5 trillion AI buildout would need to draw on every available pool of liquidity, with greater selectivity squeezing smaller and more marginal participants.

The risk assessment is also becoming more explicit in Asia. South Korea's financial watchdog asked major banks, brokerages and insurers for details of investments in and loans to AI companies, its first such request. The inquiry comes as the country's annual exports surpassed $1 trillion for the first time, supported by record semiconductor shipments. Strong equipment demand and a request to measure financial exposures are developing together.

New U.S. congressional disclosures added detail to the sector's trade exposure. A House committee said the Commerce Department approved applications covering approximately 879,000 advanced AI chips for China between December 2025 and May 2026, against requests for more than 3.4 million. Authorizations included 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, and covered Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X products.

Actual shipments under those licenses remained unclear. Nvidia said permissions carried strict conditions and limited quantities and that it had subsequently stopped H200 shipments to China; AMD said it complied with U.S. controls. Both disputed suggestions of noncompliance. Separately, Nscale will need a license to continue providing ByteDance access to Nvidia GPUs at sites including Iceland and Norway, extending the commercial significance of remote-access restrictions to those facilities.

Credit performance reflected the retreat in risk appetite. HYG returned minus 0.16% including distributions, while LQD lost 0.07%. EMB fell 0.52%. Gold futures also declined 3.05% to $3,627.90 an ounce as the dollar index edged up 0.08% to 103.938. MKS PAMP's Nicky Shiels attributed pressure on bullion partly to investors raising cash amid the AI unwind and year-end liquidity needs, alongside the effects of a hawkish Fed and stronger dollar.

## Global Rate Signals Meet French Fiscal Risk

European officials continued to make the case for higher rates while differing over how urgently to act and how much damage tighter policy could cause. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said a December increase would send a clear signal of determination to return inflation to 2%. Euro-area inflation was running at 4%, and the ECB had already raised rates twice.

Nagel also limited the comparison with the earlier energy crisis. He judged the current oil shock less severe than the gas-price surge following Russia's invasion of Ukraine and said he was not seeing a wage-price spiral. German inflation near 3% was substantially below the rates around 10% seen four years earlier, reducing the risk of second-round effects in his assessment.

Latvia's Martins Kazaks said a further small increase would probably be necessary because inflation could spread to other goods and services, while preserving a meeting-by-meeting approach. Ireland's Gabriel Makhlouf said continued evidence or the realization of inflation risks would lead him to expect another increase, consistent with his previous position. Both supplied conditional support for tightening beyond Nagel's emphasis on the signal sent by a December move.

Bank of Italy Governor Fabio Panetta emphasized preventing inflation from becoming entrenched without causing needless harm to growth. He supported the moderation of the ECB's two increases so far and had previously acknowledged that more could be necessary. Italy's October inflation had unexpectedly accelerated to 5.6%, making the balance between containment and economic damage particularly immediate in his national economy.

Austria's Martin Kocher identified an additional source of persistent price pressure. The ECB estimates that 2026 heat and drought could add 0.3-0.8 percentage point to food inflation over the next year, contributing to a projected 3.4% rate by Q3 2027. Austrian central-bank estimates put the effect of the country's hot summer on headline inflation at about 0.1 percentage point between September 2026 and June 2027. Scientific estimates also put the summer's reduction in EU GDP at approximately 0.17%, or about EUR17 billion. These estimates concern the continuing economic effects of the summer's weather, with costs on both output and prices.

Energy regulation was moving in a different direction. The EU reached a tentative agreement to postpone methane requirements for oil and natural-gas importers by two years, exceeding the one-year delay proposed by the regulator after war-related supply disruptions. The agreement changes the prospective compliance timetable as the region manages both energy security and climate-related costs.

French bonds attracted a more measured assessment from Amundi than the political anxiety visible in currency positioning. Chief investment officer Vincent Mortier said the firm remained neutral on French government debt and saw no panic selling. The 10-year yield was around 4.92% Thursday, approximately 150 basis points above Bunds, levels he considered fair given fiscal uncertainty, fundamentals and ratings.

His potential interest in additional exposure was conditional on a larger selloff without catastrophic news. October's stress had taken the yield to 5.14% and the spread to 177 basis points. Mortier said a yield around 5.3% would be difficult to ignore because it implied an inflation-adjusted yield of about 3%. He expressed confidence in the debt sustainability of France, Belgium and Italy while criticizing the combination of high debt ratios and public deficits.

Currency investors remained concerned about the presidential election and France's EUR3.6 trillion debt stock. Loomis Sayles co-head of global fixed income Lynda Schweitzer said the firm had taken a short euro position during the past month because of political unrest. Speculative bearish positions were near their highest since early 2020. Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley and Commerzbank forecast $1.08 next year; Deutsche Bank also envisaged a recovery to $1.15 by year-end as the election premium faded.

The political choices behind those views differ. Marine Le Pen, leading polls, proposed lowering retirement age as far as 60 and cutting French payments to the EU. Jean-Luc Melenchon, generally second in polls, has advocated walking away from part of the debt. Mizuho strategist Leejun Foo warned that a broader episode of OAT stress could spread across sovereign markets and increase the euro-area risk premium. The opposing Amundi assessment located substantial buying interest within the recent widening, leaving a genuine disagreement over how much fiscal risk prices already compensate.

In Britain, Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene challenged the explanation that successive external shocks alone accounted for inflation staying above target for more than five years. She argued that officials had raised rates too slowly and that policy had constrained demand less than expected. Her comments contrasted with Governor Andrew Bailey's Wednesday assessment that inflation had been on course to reach 2% this year before the Iran conflict.

The BOE increased its rate by 25 basis points to 4% this month. Investors leaned toward another December move, with an increase fully priced by February and two more by summer. Greene pointed to a stronger-than-expected economy and a stabilizing labor market, and warned that inflation above 3% could draw greater household attention and feed wage demands. In her assessment, the credibility risk from insufficient tightening exceeded the risk of doing too much. Germany's 10-year yield rose 4 basis points to 3.40% and Britain's increased 3 basis points to 5.31% in Bloomberg's session account.

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda, meanwhile, said the recent decline in consumer spending was within expectations and did not overturn his view that consumption would return to moderate growth. He expected rising nominal wages and gradually slower inflation to support real purchasing power. Pensioners were more exposed to price increases because they did not benefit from wage gains, while wage increases were spreading from large companies to smaller ones.

Overnight-indexed swaps in Tokyo Thursday assigned roughly an 84% probability to a December increase. Ueda's account kept the tightening case intact after the economic contraction, with the BOJ now seeking to maintain underlying inflation around its goal. More broadly, interest-rate futures described by Bloomberg envisaged further Fed, ECB and BOE increases through the next year, followed by largely unchanged rates at least until 2031. The combination of technology investment, defense expenditure and infrastructure borrowing was sustaining competition for funding well beyond the next meeting cycle.

## Currency Defense and Sovereign Financing Diverge

South Africa delivered a hold with a substantial minority seeking more restraint. Four members of the seven-member monetary policy committee backed leaving the rate at 7.25%, while three preferred a 25-basis-point increase. Nineteen of 20 economists surveyed by Bloomberg had expected unchanged policy. Governor Lesetja Kganyago said the bank would assess the effects of its two increases this year and remained prepared to raise rates again to return inflation to the 3% target.

The rand reversed an earlier gain after the decision and was down 1.1% by 5:30 p.m. in Johannesburg amid broader emerging-market currency weakness. The benchmark 10-year government yield nevertheless remained 6 basis points lower on the day at 8.89%. The split vote made the hold more hawkish than its headline outcome suggested.

Policymakers identified rising core inflation, a stronger dollar, higher global rates, fuel prices and El Nino as overlapping risks. One adverse scenario assumed oil peaking at $130 a barrel and limited refinery margins, leaving inflation above 5% next year and growth around 1%, potentially requiring two increases. Another considered higher global yields, rising risk premiums and a weaker rand, with similar outcomes. Those were conditional exercises used to assess risk. Bloomberg economist Yvonne Mhango still forecast 50 basis points of cuts during 2027, taking the rate to 6.75%, while Allspring's Lauren van Biljon judged additional limited tightening in Q1 possible.

Mexico's policy divide became clearer in minutes published Thursday. The peso fell 0.9% to 19.03 per dollar, its weakest since June 2025, extending its decline since early September beyond 10%. The majority of Banxico's board largely downplayed currency weakness after its recent quarter-point cut to 6.25%, according to Standard Chartered economist Dan Pan. The U.S.-Mexico rate difference had narrowed to about 237 basis points, a multiyear low, reducing the currency's carry appeal.

Dissenters Galia Borja and Jonathan Heath warned of risks to policy credibility, inflation expectations and the exchange rate. Borja argued that looser policy relative to other economies could encourage use of the peso as a hedge for global assets and amplify volatility. Most members judged core inflation to be trending lower while acknowledging upside risks. Governor Victoria Rodriguez had described the cut as a one-time action and the currency's movement as orderly, a qualification to expectations of further easing. Asset managers' bearish peso positioning had reached its largest in two decades, according to CFTC data.

Brazil's central bank took a more direct step, selling $1 billion in the spot market in its first such intervention since December 2024. The auction followed President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's statement that he was in no hurry to announce his new finance minister. The real briefly reversed its losses, then ended 1% lower at 5.94 per dollar, taking its decline since October's election to 16%. January 2029 swap rates rose as much as 51 basis points.

Asset1's Andre Shiokawa attributed the pressure to fiscal concerns and described the auction as an effort to contain volatility and the pace of depreciation. Persevera's Vinicius Marujo said the intervention's timing after Lula's remarks contributed to pressure on swaps as investors sought another outlet. On Wednesday, the Senate had backed spending restraints expected to improve the 2027 primary balance by 50 billion-60 billion reais. Investors continued to demand a larger adjustment against nominal deficits above 9% of GDP and public debt exceeding 80%.

Sovereign borrowing elsewhere demonstrated that global volatility had not closed access uniformly. China sold $2 billion of three-year dollar bonds at no spread to U.S. Treasuries, tightening from initial discussion of a roughly 25-basis-point premium. Orders exceeded $68 billion. The first Chinese sovereign dollar offering in a year repeated the zero-premium pricing achieved at the previous sale, despite international ratings below those of the United States. DBS economist Samuel Tse expected the securities to remain closely anchored to Treasury peers and described their potential appeal within Chinese dollar credit amid global uncertainty.

The Philippines raised $453.4 million at an auction of three-year retail dollar bonds paying 5.65%, returning to that format after three years. The public offer, with a $200 minimum denomination, runs through November 24. National Treasurer Sharon Almanza said proceeds would support this year's budget. The government plans borrowing of 2.73 trillion pesos this year and 3.3 trillion in 2027.

The peso traded around 63.66 per dollar Thursday afternoon in Manila, recovering from last month's record low of 64.20. Institutional buyers have dominated earlier retail dollar sales; Almanza hoped individual participation would exceed the less-than-10% share in the previous offering. The securities are expected to be less liquid than peso government bonds and global issues, an important characteristic of the government's effort to broaden its funding base.

Romania's recent bond recovery drew a conditional endorsement from Citi strategist Bhumika Gupta. The bank holds five-year leu notes bought before last month's government approval at a yield around 7.4%; that yield has since fallen to about 6.8%. Gupta saw scope for a move toward 6% if Prime Minister Luca Niculescu's minority government remained stable and delivered its fiscal plans, including a roughly 1-percentage-point reduction in the deficit relative to GDP next year.

All three major agencies assign Romania their lowest investment-grade ratings with negative outlooks. Foreign holdings relative to GDP are near decade lows, and the leu has weakened 4.8% against the euro this year. Gupta regarded fiscal and currency stability as necessary to rebuild foreign demand. She was also more cautious than Governor Mugur Isarescu's suggestion that cuts could begin as early as spring if disinflation became credible: sticky prices left her seeing little room for easing in the next six months, with limited reductions potentially possible toward late 2027 if inflation returned toward the roughly 3.7% forecast.

Gabon was seeking official support from a much weaker credit position. Finance Minister Thierry Minko targeted a staff-level IMF agreement in December and executive-board review in January. The IMF described ongoing technical engagement that could open the way to program discussions and gave no timetable, leaving a meaningful distinction between the government's objective and the lender's stated progress.

A debt audit put liabilities at $16.7 billion, nearly a fifth below initial estimates, or 69% of GDP. That brought the ratio within CEMAC's 70% ceiling. More immediately, lawmakers adopted a revised budget Wednesday projecting a 2027 primary surplus of 0.6% of non-rebased GDP, replacing a proposed 1.3% deficit. Minko said consultation with IMF staff informed the changes; the government projects larger surpluses of 2.1% in 2028 and 2.5% in 2029.

Minko said proceeds from October's eurobond had cleared approximately EUR47 million of African Development Bank arrears and that about EUR15 million owed to the Islamic Development Bank had also been settled. Clearance of remaining World Bank arrears was being finalized. Gabon raised $920 million privately in July and $580 million publicly in October, using proceeds for external debt and infrastructure.

The revised framework permits up to 1.04 trillion CFA francs, or $1.7 billion, of international financing. Minko said another eurobond was one possible component alongside regional borrowing, bank finance, project loans and development support, with no firm new issue amount. Gabon's 2034 notes were issued at 12.8%, and its sovereign spread stood at 824 basis points in intraday JPMorgan index data, second in Africa to Senegal's 1,529. Minko argued that investors were applying an excessive, insufficiently differentiated African risk premium; Fitch's CCC- rating underscored the country's still-fragile credit standing.

Zimbabwe pursued a different route to official financing, asking the World Bank, African Development Bank and European Investment Bank for grants or loans to clear arrears owed to those same institutions. Its finance ministry said grants and long-term concessional funding were the most sustainable option alongside reform and transparency. The country owes $21.7 billion overall, including arrears of $1.7 billion to the World Bank, $835 million to the African Development Bank and $433 million to the EIB. Those overdue obligations prevent access to new facilities. Previous requests to third countries for bridge finance had failed, and the new requests remained unresolved.

## Refinancings and Restructurings Reorder Creditor Claims

Corporate transactions showed a range of ways borrowers were securing liquidity or changing the allocation of losses. Australian coking-coal miner GM3 obtained an agreement from an RRJ Capital-led consortium to purchase $619 million of five-year bonds, replacing a planned public offering after volatility and wider spreads made distribution more difficult. Proceeds will refinance a $600 million private-credit loan. The notes are scheduled to be issued December 8, carry a 9.75% coupon, were sold at 97 and become callable in 2028.

The refinancing replaces financing associated with GM3's acquisition from South32 in 2024. The existing loan was provided by Deutsche Bank and private-credit funds including Davidson Kempner and Farallon. The move to a private placement secured committed buyers on specified terms while leaving the issuance date ahead.

Italian luxury group Tod's was nearing a EUR400 million bank refinancing supported by a conditional commitment from the Della Valle family. The proposed package comprises a EUR200 million term loan, a EUR100 million revolver and a EUR100 million capital-expenditure line. Maturity would extend by one year to the end of 2031, and financial covenants would be reset. Intesa Sanpaolo, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole, UniCredit and Banco BPM were among the lenders.

The family's equity support of up to EUR60 million would be triggered if specified financial targets were missed. Tod's said it was finalizing plans with its longstanding banks, without confirming the detailed terms. The proposed flexibility follows a 7.7% revenue decline to EUR966.4 million in 2025 and a 16% fall in EBITDA to EUR144.7 million. Net debt was EUR578 million including leases, or EUR122 million excluding them, compared with EUR645 million and EUR141 million respectively in 2024. The lease distinction materially changes the scale of the reported debt burden.

Rakuten confronted a different threat to financing costs before a planned roughly JPY150 billion subordinated offering. Spreads on JPY360 billion of retail bonds issued in October widened to about 212 basis points over government debt by November 18, the highest since issuance. A bond due in August 2028 widened 12 basis points in a day to a post-issue high.

Rakuten Securities had said data from as many as 4.47 million customer accounts might have leaked, including names, addresses, income and financial assets. S&P said November 19 that cyber incidents in Japan were producing tangible operating effects and that compensation and support costs could significantly affect earnings and cash flow. Rakuten Bank shares fell again Thursday to JPY4,281 after the prior day's limit-down decline. The potential costs come alongside the group's continuing mobile-business losses and repeated use of debt markets.

Japan Tobacco quantified an already-realized loss of control over Russian businesses. It will take a JPY1.4 trillion, or $8.9 billion, charge after Moscow seized seven subsidiaries. Russia accounted for about 10% of revenue and a quarter of adjusted operating profit. The charge will push the group to a full-year loss and halve its year-end dividend, showing the disproportionate earnings importance of the affected operations.

In U.S. structured finance, Crunch Fitness assembled an $800 million whole-business financing backed by franchise agreements and assets including intellectual property. The package included $650 million of bonds with an average life of about five years, a $100 million privately placed note drawable later and a $50 million variable funding facility. KBRA rated it BBB-, the lowest investment-grade level. The largest portion sold at a 7.39% yield, 2.5 percentage points above benchmarks, with proceeds intended for refinancing and operating cash reserves.

The structure joins a run of franchise-backed transactions, including Neighborly's $275 million offering. Its mix of issued bonds and contingent facilities gives Crunch different forms of financing capacity within the headline package. Guggenheim was sole structuring adviser and lead bookrunner, with other banks participating in distribution.

Vivid Seats disclosed a restructuring that would transfer 80% of its equity to lenders and leave existing shareholders with about 20%. The creditors will provide a $66 million first-lien, first-out term loan, while net debt is set to fall by approximately $232 million and leverage to about three times from nine times. People familiar with the transaction identified Blackstone, Shenkman, Oaktree, GDA Luma and Carlyle among the lenders.

The take-back debt includes a 66% change-of-control premium, requiring repayment at 166% of principal upon a sale. That contractual protection is important to the lenders' prospective return as they exchange their position for a combination of debt and control. The existing $387 million term loan due in 2029 was most recently quoted around 50 cents on the dollar. Shares rose 63% Thursday after gaining as much as 105% intraday.

The operating backdrop remained difficult. Q3 resale orders were 97,000 against expectations above 104,000, although adjusted EBITDA of $8.87 million beat estimates. Competitors have been spending heavily on marketing, and a District of Columbia law limiting resale prices and fees is due to take effect in January. Resellers are challenging that law in court. Separately, lenders to Scientific Games organized with Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher and signed a cooperation pact open to all participants, according to people familiar with the matter.

The sale of debt on Syracuse's Destiny USA mall highlighted an older capital structure's repayment priorities. Namdar Realty became lender of record after developer Pyramid Management failed to close an earlier accepted bid for the property's $430 million of commercial mortgage debt. Pyramid had sought to buy it for less than 20 cents on the dollar; that failed bid does not establish Namdar's purchase price.

The mall's latest appraisal, from 2023, was $133 million, down 81% from 2014. Its highest CMBS tranche, originally rated AAA, trades around 17 cents on the dollar. Approximately $235 million of municipal bonds backed by payments in lieu of taxes remain outstanding and continue to receive payments. Those securities, issued before the CMBS, have priority for repayment despite having carried a lower rating when the mortgage securities were sold. The priority limits the claims of mortgage bondholders against a property already struggling with weaker retail demand and prohibitive refinancing costs.

## Forward Market Significance

The November 25 U.S. releases will bring Q3 GDP's second estimate and corporate profits alongside October personal income and outlays, all scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Eastern. The combination will add information on growth, company earnings, household spending and inflation after Thursday's weaker claims and Philadelphia observations. For the December 8-9 FOMC meeting, Goolsbee's concern about seasonal reacceleration puts the persistence of price pressure alongside the size of the next increase; Jefferson's framework leaves the response sensitive to employment and inflation expectations as well as current investment demand.

China's November 20 lending-rate decision remains pending. In a Reuters survey, 23 of 28 participants expected the one-year and five-year loan prime rates to stay at 3.00% and 3.50%, while five anticipated a cut in one or both. The emergence of a minority expecting immediate easing broke several months of unanimous hold forecasts. An unchanged decision would extend the pause to 18 months. Earlier November changes to the PBOC's operating framework effectively lowered the floor of its rate corridor by 15 basis points; Citi nevertheless expected no November LPR cut and forecast two 10-basis-point reductions in 2027.

Fresh research adds a longer-running employment issue to that policy assessment. Bloomberg's analysis of nearly 10 million Chinese online job postings found hiring in occupations more exposed to AI falling about 10 percentage points more than in less-exposed work. The finding comes with limited official information and companies' reluctance to attribute job cuts to AI. It raises a separate question about the durability of household demand as officials assess easing, distinct from the current strength of equipment investment. In Japan, Friday's inflation release is expected to show the key gauge accelerating to its fastest pace this year; Ueda speaks November 30 before the December 18 policy decision.

Nearer-term credit tests include Fitch's Friday review of Gabon and the Philippines' retail dollar subscription period through November 24. Gabon's pending IMF engagement leaves the government's December agreement target dependent on further technical and policy progress. Romania's next ratings assessment comes from Fitch in January, testing whether the new government's fiscal program is restoring credibility. South Africa's next scheduled rate decision is January 28, leaving a lengthy interval for the dollar, core inflation and energy prices to change the balance exposed by its narrow hold vote.

North American trade negotiations carry an additional cost risk into January. In an account published just after U.S. bond trading ended, Reuters cited participants in a November 19 Canadian advisory briefing who said Washington had made little meaningful movement on tariff relief since talks broke down in August. Tariffs affecting Canadian steel, automobiles and lumber are scheduled to rise from 25% to 50% in January 2027. Industry groups warned of supply-chain disruption, closures and job losses if the increases take effect. LeBlanc's office confirmed the briefing and continued pursuit of an agreement, while participants said the U.S. midterms had not materially changed the negotiating position.

For AI financing, the return of the postponed Alphabet-linked municipal deals and the prospective SpaceX distribution will test demand in markets with different investors and structures. Their pending terms matter after a session in which a record equity offering, a completed Canadian bond sale and delayed municipal transactions produced sharply different outcomes. In energy, the Shenzhen supply pledge leaves the operational question with production and transport as military risks around Hormuz remain active.

Softer U.S. data coexisted with Fed warnings about persistent inflation and AI-driven demand. Lower real yields drove most of the bond rally, while U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably and Alphabet's completed Canadian sale contrasted with postponed municipal financing.

section_summaries.summary: Anthropic's record fundraising and strong debut failed to halt the wider technology selloff. Alphabet sold C$6 billion of Canadian bonds, but $3 billion of linked prepaid-energy municipal deals were postponed as investors sought better pricing. CoreWeave defended reinvesting cash in computing capacity with unsecured debt yielding roughly 15%, while SpaceX considered a debt sale of at least $32 billion. section_summaries.summary: ECB officials supported further tightening with differing views on urgency and growth costs; the BOE's Greene argued policy had constrained demand too little, while Ueda retained his consumption outlook. French fiscal risk divided investors: Amundi remained neutral on government debt around a 150-basis-point spread to Bunds, while currency investors positioned for election-related euro weakness. European yields rose in the session account.

section_summaries.section_title: Currency Defense and Sovereign Financing Diverge
section_summaries.summary: South Africa held at 7.25% in a narrow vote, Banxico's minutes exposed concern over the peso after its cut, and Brazil's $1 billion intervention failed to prevent a lower real close. Sovereign access varied: China sold $2 billion of dollar bonds at no spread to Treasuries, while the Philippines reopened retail dollar funding. Gabon targeted a December IMF agreement, but the lender described technical engagement without a timetable; Zimbabwe's arrears-financing requests remained unresolved.

section_summaries.section_title: Refinancings and Restructurings Reorder Creditor Claims
section_summaries.summary: GM3 secured buyers for $619 million of private bonds after abandoning a public offering, while Tod's neared a EUR400 million bank refinancing with conditional family support. Vivid Seats' restructuring would give lenders 80% of equity and reduce net debt by about $232 million, with a 166%-of-principal repayment requirement on a sale. At Destiny USA, earlier municipal debt retained repayment priority over distressed mortgage claims.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries rally as the equity reversal exposes strains in AI financing
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries gained as early enthusiasm for Anthropic's debut gave way to a broad equity selloff. The 2-year yield fell 4.24 basis points to 4.7618%, while the 10-year declined 2.22 basis points to 5.0461%, steepening the curve. Lower real yields accounted for most of the 10-year move: the TIPS yield fell 1.8 basis points, with breakeven inflation down only 0.42 basis point as oil recovered. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably.

Continuing jobless claims rose more than expected and Philadelphia manufacturing slowed sharply, although that survey's input prices accelerated and Kansas City activity strengthened. Goolsbee kept a larger December increase open for discussion, warning that AI investment could exceed near-term productive capacity. Jefferson likewise separated its immediate inflationary demand from productivity gains that could arrive later.

Anthropic raised $107.3 billion through its IPO and a private placement, and its shares closed 17% above the offering price. That success did not restore broader confidence: the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.21% after reversing an early rally. Alphabet completed a C$6 billion Canadian bond sale, while $3 billion of Alphabet-linked prepaid-energy municipal offerings were postponed over demand and pricing. The contrasting outcomes left access to funding and its cost central to the AI buildout. The return of those municipal deals and a prospective SpaceX debt sale will test borrowing appetite beyond the equity debut.
